body:
## Pull request overview

Adds a new set of metadata CRUD AI tools to `@objectstack/service-ai`, implementing tool definitions (`AIToolDefinition`) and runtime handlers in one place (mirroring the existing `data-tools.ts` pattern), plus unit tests and documentation updates.

**Changes:**
- Introduces `metadata-tools.ts` with 6 metadata management tools and a `registerMetadataTools()` helper.
- Exports the new registration helper/definitions from `service-ai` public entrypoints.
- Adds a dedicated vitest suite for the new tools and updates `CHANGELOG.md` / `ROADMAP.md`.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 6 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated 9 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| ROADMAP.md | Marks metadata management tools milestone as complete. |
| CHANGELOG.md | Documents the addition of metadata management tools and tests. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/tools/metadata-tools.ts | Adds 6 metadata tool definitions + handlers + registration helper. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/tools/index.ts | Re-exports metadata tools from the tools barrel. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/index.ts | Re-exports metadata tools from the package public API. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/__tests__/metadata-tools.test.ts | Adds unit tests covering the metadata tool handlers and lifecycle. |
</details>

`LIST_OBJECTS_TOOL` reuses the tool name `list_objects`, which is already defined and registered by `data-tools.ts`. If an app registers both data tools and metadata tools on the same `ToolRegistry`, the later registration will overwrite the earlier one (ToolRegistry uses Map.set), breaking existing agents/features that rely on the original `list_objects` output shape. Please rename these metadata tools (or make their parameter/output contract fully backward-compatible with the existing `list_objects` tool).
```suggestion
  name: 'list_metadata_objects',
  description:
    'Lists all registered metadata data objects (tables) in the current environment. ' +
    'Use this when the user wants to see what tables, entities, or data models are defined in metadata.',
```

`DESCRIBE_OBJECT_TOOL` also reuses the existing `describe_object` tool name from `data-tools.ts`, but returns a different response shape (fields array + enableFeatures) than the current data tool (fields map). Registering both tool sets will cause one to clobber the other and can break the built-in `data_chat` agent/tests. Consider renaming the metadata variant or aligning its response format with the existing `describe_object` contract.

`add_field` defines `reference` as an object with `{ object, labelField }`, but the core Field schema in `@objectstack/spec` uses `reference` as a string target object name (e.g. `reference: 'account'`). Persisting an object here will produce object definitions that don’t match the platform’s canonical shape. Suggest changing this parameter to `reference: string` (and, if needed, add separate optional fields like `referenceLabelField` rather than changing the type of `reference`).

Handler input typing for `add_field` treats `reference` as `{ object: string; labelField?: string }` and later stores it directly into the field definition. This will write an invalid field shape relative to the spec (`reference` should be a string). Update the handler to accept/store a string reference (and validate it as snake_case) to avoid creating metadata that downstream schema validation/publish flows will reject.

`create_object` builds `fieldMap` from the `fields` array without validating each field’s `name` (snake_case), presence, or duplicates. With invalid/missing names, this can silently create keys like `'undefined'` or overwrite earlier fields in the loop. Add per-field validation (same snake_case regex), check for duplicates, and return a clear error before registering the object.

`add_field` validates the new field’s `name` but does not validate `objectName` as snake_case (even though the tool contract describes it that way). Adding a simple regex validation for `objectName` (and similarly for `fieldName`/`objectName` in modify/delete/describe) would prevent confusing lookups like `getObject('MyObject')` and make errors consistent.

`modify_field` description says it can “rename” a column, but the handler only shallow-merges `changes` into the existing field object and keeps the field map key unchanged. If `changes` includes `name`, this will not actually rename the field (and can leave key/name inconsistent). Either remove “rename” from the description or implement a real rename that updates the fields map key (and related references like indexes/nameField if applicable).
```suggestion
    'Use this when the user wants to change or reconfigure an existing column or attribute (not rename it).',
```

For `select` field options, the spec requires option `value` to be a lowercase machine identifier. The tool schema currently only types it as `string`, and the handler passes values through unvalidated. Consider validating/normalizing option values (e.g., enforce lowercase snake_case) to prevent registering metadata that later fails schema validation.
```suggestion
            value: {
              type: 'string',
              description: 'Option machine identifier (lowercase snake_case, e.g. high_priority)',
              pattern: '^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$',
            },
```

Current tests only cover registering metadata tools in isolation. Given that `list_objects` and `describe_object` collide with existing data tool names, please add a test that registers both `registerDataTools` and `registerMetadataTools` on the same `ToolRegistry` and asserts the intended behavior (either no collisions due to renames, or explicit override semantics). This will prevent accidental regressions in tool registration order.
